# Exact-commit CI evidence: f5484b9f

This record belongs to `f5484b9ff80ebae9c728204c48387e3ef148bda8`.
[The JSON record](./f5484b9f-ci.json) preserves two new run IDs, 21 job IDs,
17 artifact metadata records and 30 independently checked core-file hashes.
Original downloads remain under `/tmp/beautiful-ci-f5484b9f`. Both runs ended
naturally; neither was retried or cancelled.

| Run | Result | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Main 33834459633](https://github.com/pawaovo/shadcn_flutter/actions/runs/33834459633) | **11/12 jobs passed; actual iOS and Android journeys passed** | The only failed job is Edge's original journey, which timed out during initial window positioning at `about:blank`, before application assertions. |
| [Input/AT 33834459596](https://github.com/pawaovo/shadcn_flutter/actions/runs/33834459596) | **4/9 combined jobs passed; trusted W3C 4/4 passed** | Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari completed the full independent trusted-input suite. All three native framework/clipboard targets and ordinary GTK Orca capability passed. |

The real iOS report records `passed=true`, with its required Dart driver exiting
zero after 57.405 seconds. The original log records `All tests passed.`. This
complete journey includes both unconditional FineTune checks at
`catalog_journey_test.dart:271-282`: controller text equals `'360'` and actual
host settings width equals `360`. The assertions verify these values; the log
does not print them individually. VM capture also reports clean host process
ownership, stdout EOF and a completed final drain. Android's original full
journey passes, including asynchronous copy feedback. These are new successful
results for this exact candidate, distinct from the earlier iOS failures.

All four independent W3C suites completed Prompt, keyboard, real browser resize
and clipboard checks, including readonly copy, Cut rejection, caret collapse,
Paste rejection and final completion. Safari's separate original full journey
also passed. Chrome and Firefox's retained framework checks still lost an
injected composing range; Safari passed Prompt composition and numeric
scenarios but lost the range during synthetic resize. These injected checks do
not establish an OS IME defect or OS IME acceptance.

Both Edge failures occurred before application assertions: main's initial
`POST /session/.../window/rect` with `{x:0,y:0}` returned HTTP 500 after 300.098
seconds; the separate framework suite's same initial request failed after
300.067 seconds, with its diagnostic URL still `about:blank`. That framework
suite produced no assertion report. The independent fresh Edge W3C suite in
the same input job passed. Main and input ran different Edge versions, so
their results are not presented as a same-binary comparison. No timeout,
argument, positioning request or acceptance condition was changed to turn
these failures into passes.

The [bounded startup comparison](../../docs/beautiful-ui/quality_evidence/2026-09-04-edge-startup-boundary.md)
also confirms that the successful suite executed the same SDK position request.
The failed request was waiting for initial navigation and had not reached the
actual bounds-setting command; no configuration difference or specific resource
cause was established.

No new Catalog Orca pilot was dispatched. A verified empty commit-to-commit
diff covers the entire public package, Catalog production Dart and all six
platform source trees between `e3526d3f` and this candidate. The
[e3526d3f native evidence](./e3526d3f-ci.md) is therefore retained explicitly as
historical evidence for unchanged runtime sources: the actual FlView bridge
cases and JSON report passed, while complete Catalog AT tasks remained 0/3
accepted. The [Linux SDK boundary report](../../docs/beautiful-ui/quality_evidence/2026-09-04-linux-sdk-accessibility-boundaries.md)
documents dynamic-name and expanded-state mapping gaps. That historical pilot
is not counted as a new run for this SHA.

Narrator again lacked a usable WASAPI render endpoint (`0x80070490`) despite
native accessibility and ordinary keyboard response. Full application AT
acceptance, human speech review, physical-device acceptance and OS IME
acceptance remain unestablished. The main and input workflows retain their
actual failure conclusions alongside the passing application and W3C results.
